one_line: A provenance-first activity index for hashtags across Mastodon-compatible servers.
what_it_does: Polls decentralized hashtag timelines, deduplicates observations, reports coverage/freshness/comparability, and gives agents calibrated evidence.
leverage_rationale: Required provenance, standing, coverage, freshness, and insufficient-data statuses prevent agents from dropping caveats that screen reading would lose.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly says tools carry provenance and refuse unsupported trends.
Observed data is separated from sightings and server counters.
execution_rationale: The methodology and refusal behavior are coherent and unusually explicit, but no runtime sequence is demonstrated in the packet.
execution_evidence: Description details polling, deduplication, health, coverage, and comparable slices.
Facts report a live demo link.
impact_rationale: Journalists, researchers, moderators, and fediverse users need trustworthy activity estimates in a decentralized network.
impact_evidence: Clear problem: no central server can provide complete counts.
Answers retain source servers, coverage, freshness, and reasons for insufficient data.
creativity_rationale: Making calibrated refusal and evidence provenance the product's core agent interaction is a novel, principled use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: The tool changes what an agent can honestly say, not merely how it clicks.
Index treats incompleteness as a first-class result.
usability_note: Evidence-forward answers can build trust; decentralized terminology may require explanation.
red_flags: Claims are methodologically strong but unverified by transcript/frame evidence.
standouts: Excellent evidence-integrity framing and refusal semantics.
advance_reason: High-quality WebMCP rationale tied to a real decentralized-data problem.

one_line: A provenance-aware research system linking experiments, evidence, and manuscript claims with agent verification.
what_it_does: Tracks experiment lineage, links evidence to paper objects, detects stale/contradicted claims, and exposes verification and research-diff workflows through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: Structured bidirectional research state and deterministic claim verification are substantially more reliable than an agent navigating a paper editor and manually inferring provenance.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies experiments, typed evidence, linked claims/methods/tables/figures, stale propagation, Verify This, and Research Diff.
Frame sheets are submitted for the core editor and provenance workflows.
execution_rationale: The stated lifecycle and signature experiences are unusually complete, and gallery/frame evidence supports a real editor with research state; exact agent calls and final corrections are not fully legible.
execution_evidence: Eight gallery images and three frame sheets are claimed.
Description specifies planned/running/completed/failed/superseded states and multiple drift views.
No transcript and detailed result text is small.
impact_rationale: Researchers have a real reproducibility and manuscript-drift problem; linking claims to evidence and flagging stale results directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Clear research audience and concrete failure mode: papers copied results manually and become stale.
Deterministic verification and reviewable diffs support credible scholarly workflows.
creativity_rationale: The software-dependency-graph approach to papers, evidence, and research diffs is genuinely novel and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Research X-Ray, Verify This, and Research Diff form a coherent original interaction suite.
Bidirectional run-to-paper and paper-to-run provenance is memorable.
usability_note: The workflow is conceptually rigorous and editor-oriented; evidence is insufficient to assess polish of all states.
red_flags: Agent invocation details are not readable in the frame sheets.
Broad research lifecycle claims exceed what can be independently observed from stills.
standouts: Treats manuscript drift like code drift with reviewable diffs.
Deterministic numeric claim verification avoids silent hallucinated corrections.
advance_reason: Exceptional research fit, originality, and coherent execution evidence make this a clear advance.

one_line: An explorable pixel-art portfolio shared by visitors and page-aware agents.
what_it_does: Provides an HD-2D world, landmark navigation, personalized tours, page-specific inspection, biography/research tools, and explicit human-controlled copying.
leverage_rationale: Page-aware tools and shared route state improve agent navigation and context, though a general agent could reproduce much of the browsing outcome with friction.
leverage_evidence: Global and page-specific tools move with the visible route and expose the same interface state.
Agent can create goal-specific tours and walk the on-screen traveler to landmarks.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent portfolio world and rights-safe competition edition with multiple interaction modes; frame sheets are available but end-to-end video proof is absent.
execution_evidence: Keyboard, mouse, touch, and agent navigation are all described.
Sanitized Mods page and explicit human-only copying show deliberate packaging and boundaries.
impact_rationale: Recruiters, collaborators, technical reviewers, and creative visitors have a credible need for tailored portfolio exploration.
impact_evidence: Goal-specific tours address differing visitor information needs.
Research tools provide publication metadata and paste-ready BibTeX.
creativity_rationale: A memorable playable portfolio/world as an agent-human shared interface is highly original and pursued deeply.
creativity_evidence: Visitors and agents inhabit the same navigable pixel world.
Page-aware tool registration changes with route and content context.
usability_note: Multiple input modes and landmarks support exploration, but a game-like portfolio may add discovery friction.
red_flags: The packet says it began as a personal hub world, so the competition extension is meaningful but not wholly new.
standouts: Rights-safe sanitization and human-controlled copying are thoughtful.
advance_reason: Highly creative, coherent shared-world portfolio with credible agent-aware navigation.

one_line: Causal Mission Gate turns intent into governed, auditable agent missions.
what_it_does: Creates versioned mission contracts, manages autonomy and escalation, gates critical effects on exact human approval, and verifies receipts.
leverage_rationale: The product is built around structured agent governance: exact intent digests, version checks, bounded tools, and human-only authority actions are difficult to reproduce comparably through generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: 11 bounded WebMCP tools
Human authority actions excluded from agent tools
Frame shows intent to structured resumable delegation and APPROVED state
Server validates version and intent digest
execution_rationale: The UI and description align around a serious governance workflow with visible staged approval, but no video/transcript and limited direct end-to-end proof cap confidence.
execution_evidence: Frames show populated mission/delegation states
Approval is visibly represented
No submitted video or transcript
impact_rationale: Teams deploying agents have a concrete need to separate capability from authority and retain auditability for consequential actions.
impact_evidence: Mission contracts define success, reversibility, and escalation
Receipts and audit-chain verification described
Critical effects require exact approval
creativity_rationale: The exact-intent, single-use, time-limited approval model is an ambitious and distinctive interaction/governance design.
creativity_evidence: Capability does not imply authority principle
Approval bound to mission/version/digest
Management-by-exception operating profile
usability_note: Dark structured UI communicates state, though dense controls may be demanding.
red_flags: Claims of audit-chain verification are not directly observable in frames
standouts: Human authority is deliberately absent from agent tool surface
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and a coherent, high-impact governance concept.

one_line: Council-service workspace where an agent adapts the interface and drafts housing repairs while the resident remains in control.
what_it_does: Lets residents use natural language to adapt a council-services UI, prepare a housing-repair request, review it, and submit only after human confirmation; the persisted repair then appears in staff workflow.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP materially enables shared human-agent state: the agent can adapt the live interface and update the same repair draft the resident sees, with a deliberate human-only submission boundary.
leverage_evidence: About text describes six structured tools and the same live housing-repair draft visible and editable by the resident.
About text claims 11/11 natural-language tool-selection and safety scenarios passed.
Frame sheet shows a WebMCP interaction panel and page state, but visible failure states limit certainty.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent resident-to-staff workflow with safety gating and persistence, but end-to-end execution is claimed rather than demonstrated by a submitted video.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive and the description specifies draft, confirmation, submission, reference generation, and staff inbox persistence.
Frame evidence shows the product UI and WebMCP panel, though the contact sheet appears to include error states.
No video transcript or actual video is supplied.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete accessibility and public-service problem for residents with varied abilities and preferences, while preserving human agency over consequential submission.
impact_evidence: Description identifies council-service accessibility barriers and a resident/staff repair use case.
The workflow supports larger text, larger controls, simpler language, and stepwise completion.
creativity_rationale: The human-agent collaboration model treats adaptive interface presentation and shared state as the product, rather than merely adding an agent button to a form.
creativity_evidence: Pitch centers Humans × Agents and agent adaptation of the same resident-facing interface.
Human-only confirmation and staff-side persisted reference are integrated into the concept.
usability_note: The stated adaptive controls and review gate are strong, though visible contact-sheet errors reduce confidence in polish.
red_flags: No submitted video despite frame-sheet artifacts; contact sheet appears to show failed interactions.
Execution and final persistence are primarily claimed.
standouts: Shared live state between resident and agent.
Human-only final submission with staff inbox continuity.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-specific shared-state and accessibility concept with credible impact; advance despite limited execution evidence.

one_line: A newsroom workspace where agents help move stories through editorial, media-rights, and publishing gates.
what_it_does: Manages story lifecycle, media licensing and accessibility metadata, validation, human approval, and publishing handoff through 22 tools.
leverage_rationale: Agents can inspect and mutate connected editorial and rights state, detect blockers, and prepare a validated publishing payload more reliably than UI automation.
leverage_evidence: 22 real WebMCP tools span story, media vault, rights, validation, and handoff.
Expired image license blocks an otherwise approved story.
Publishing occurs only after validation and human approval.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, intentionally bounded newsroom workflow with visible product areas and frame sheets; the central blocker-resolution path appears complete.
execution_evidence: Story Desk, Media Vault, and Handoff Engine are connected.
Frame sheets and screenshot supplied.
Rights and accessibility validation are part of the stated workflow.
impact_rationale: Editorial teams have a real coordination and compliance burden, and preventing rights or accessibility failures before publishing is valuable.
impact_evidence: Targets assignment through publishing handoff.
Explicit licensing, attribution, accessibility, and approval requirements.
creativity_rationale: The concept goes beyond an agent writing text: it makes a newsroom's operational state and publishing gates agent-native.
creativity_evidence: Media-rights blocker resolution is a specific, memorable workflow.
Agent and editor collaborate on the same editorial pipeline.
usability_note: The domain model is rich and review gates support safe adoption, though 22 tools may increase complexity.
red_flags: No transcript and no independent confirmation of publishing integration.
Scope breadth may leave edge cases unfinished.
standouts: Strong shared state across human editorial work and agent actions.
advance_reason: Deep, coherent agent-native workflow with clear operational value and strong evidence surfaces.

one_line: A workbench that verifies whether WebMCP tools behave as their descriptions and annotations claim.
what_it_does: Discovers tools, generates safe inputs, invokes them in disposable browser sessions, records output and side effects, and shows diffs, network activity, and logs.
leverage_rationale: The product directly tests the structured agent surface itself; isolated invocation, schema-aware inputs, and observable side-effect diffs are impractical to reproduce comparably with a general UI-driving agent.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies discovery, schemas, annotations, synthetic inputs, isolated invocation, browser-state diffs, network activity, and runtime logs.
The workbench exposes its own structured tools for inspecting and rerunning verification.
Frame sheets show a dedicated verification UI and evidence-oriented workflow.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete, internally coherent testing workflow and the submitted frames show a workbench with evidence surfaces, though all test cases are not independently verified.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show landing/workbench states and verification evidence UI.
About text describes the end-to-end disposable-browser workflow.
demo_alive is reported alive and public repository is present.
impact_rationale: Developers and agent operators have a real need to detect tool side effects, misleading annotations, and unreliable behavior before deployment.
impact_evidence: About text gives the concrete read-only-but-mutating tool failure mode.
Outputs include suggested repair plus timeline, state diff, network, and runtime evidence.
creativity_rationale: It turns WebMCP from merely an integration surface into an auditable subject of verification, with a compelling evidence model for humans and agents.
creativity_evidence: The product verifies claims against observed browser behavior rather than trusting metadata.
Disposable execution and evidence workbench are a strong, memorable interaction model.
usability_note: A timeline/diff/log workbench gives developers actionable evidence; safe-input generation reduces setup burden.
red_flags: The frames show the verification interface, but do not prove every advertised side-effect detector works across arbitrary sites.
standouts: Directly addresses trustworthiness of WebMCP tools.
Strong evidence-oriented product surface rather than a thin tool list.
advance_reason: High leverage, strong developer impact, and unusually original WebMCP-specific concept.

one_line: A stateful text adventure where an AI Dungeon Master acts through five bounded tools.
what_it_does: Provides a playable dungeon with real game state; the agent reads state, spawns encounters, resolves combat, awards items, and advances story through tools that can be refused.
leverage_rationale: The agent is an actual constrained game actor operating canonical state, not merely narrating; refusal and rule validation make tool use materially different from chat narration.
leverage_evidence: Five tools are the DM's only way into the game
Tools can reject invalid or premature actions
Every call changes the player's visible state
execution_rationale: Seven gallery images describe a progression from broken gate through combat, rewards, and ending, suggesting a coherent playable arc; no video means claims are not directly observed.
execution_evidence: Public repo and live demo reported
Gallery covers multiple story and difficulty states plus phone view
Real game state and rule enforcement are central claims
impact_rationale: Players who want responsive AI-assisted tabletop-style fiction can get meaningful entertainment and replay value.
impact_evidence: Clear playable audience and concrete dungeon loop
Stateful rules address a known weakness of purely narrated AI DMs
creativity_rationale: Making the AI DM an accountable tool-mediated actor rather than an omnipotent narrator is a strong interaction concept.
creativity_evidence: Page can refuse the DM
Rules, dice/state, and narrative are separated while still collaborating
usability_note: Buttons plus free-form play should be approachable; refusal feedback is important to learnability.
red_flags: No video or transcript; tool invocation and full gameplay are inferred from gallery/description
standouts: Refusal behavior is a memorable proof of real state
advance_reason: Creative, category-appropriate game with meaningful agent leverage and a credible state model.

one_line: Temporary capability borrowing with human approval and one-time access.
what_it_does: Connects an agent browser and capability-holder browser so an agent can discover manifests, request private capabilities, receive one-time approved payloads, and be revoked.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP plus browser-to-browser transfer creates a capability lifecycle and consent boundary that generic UI automation cannot replicate comparably well.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies discover/request/approve/borrow/revoke lifecycle.
Private payload is hidden during discovery and one-time approval consumes access.
Frames show populated two-sided relay/dashboard states.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent security lifecycle and shows multiple dashboard states, but the actual approved transfer is not legible.
execution_evidence: Written build includes WebRTC DataChannel and human permission request.
Frame sheets show agent/task/capability panels.
impact_rationale: Temporary least-privilege access solves a real problem in agent integrations where persistent permissions are risky.
impact_evidence: Concrete private note, file, JSON, and page-context capabilities.
Explicit deny, approve-once, and end-forget controls.
creativity_rationale: Borrowing capabilities as temporary authority is a memorable and original interaction/security model.
creativity_evidence: Capability holder retains control while agent discovers only a manifest.
Direct browser-to-browser one-time transfer and revocation.
usability_note: Two-browser lifecycle is conceptually clear but operationally more complex than a single-page tool.
red_flags: No readable payload transfer or approval trace in frames.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP/security concept with clear real-world value and originality.

one_line: A WebMCP storefront where agents discover paid AI services and humans approve x402 payment.
what_it_does: Lists services, exposes pricing and inputs, lets ChatGPT request a paid service, pauses at HTTP 402, and resumes after explicit human wallet approval with results returned to the agent.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central to live service discovery, structured request inputs, payment gating, and returning results in the agent flow; generic UI driving would be materially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Description states eight live WebMCP tools for service discovery, pricing, requests, and result checks.
Claimed flow stops at 402 until human approval, then settles x402 and returns result.
Frames show Agent Shop service catalog and activity panel.
execution_rationale: The narrative and packaging describe a complete paid-request lifecycle and frames show a coherent storefront, but no video transcript or directly readable completed trace is available.
execution_evidence: Devpost preview visibly shows priced services, Market Search, and Agent activity.
Description gives a specific JSON Repair request lifecycle.
No direct readable payment/result execution log in supplied images.
impact_rationale: Agent-accessible small paid services with human-controlled spending address a real gap in agent commerce and preserve meaningful user consent.
impact_evidence: Concrete service catalog with USDC prices.
Explicit human approval boundary before wallet payment.
Results are intended to return directly to the requesting agent.
creativity_rationale: The combination of a live agent storefront, x402 payments, and a deliberate human approval checkpoint is an original and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent discovers and requests services rather than merely automating a page.
Payment stops at 402 and requires visible human continuation.
usability_note: Catalog/pricing and activity visibility support understandable use; payment and wallet setup add friction but appropriately for safety.
red_flags: Project explicitly says the Agent Shop existed before the challenge.
Video frames are mostly repeated and do not independently verify completed payment.
standouts: Strong WebMCP-as-product, not just a UI button.
advance_reason: One of the clearest central WebMCP use cases: discover, request, gate payment, and return a structured service result.
